James Ussher (1658), p. 47; Edward Mack, ISBE (1915), p. 640; R. C. Young's tables

All three reckonings make Jehoram of Judah king alongside his father Jehoshaphat, so the same year was Jehoshaphat's eighteenth and Jehoram's second; Ussher calls it making him “Vice-Roy”, Mack “coregency”, and Young dates it from 854 BC.[2][21][1]
2 Kings 1 2 Kings 3 2 Kings 5 2 Kings 6 2 Kings 7 2 Kings 8 2 Kings 9 2 Chronicles 22
2 Kings 1:17–18 2 Kings 3:1–27 2 Kings 5:5–8 2 Kings 6:8–7:20 2 Kings 8:1–6 2 Kings 8:16 2 Kings 8:25–29 2 Kings 9:14–26 2 Chronicles 22:5–7
Kings gives no “rest of the acts” note and no burial for Joram; his body was left on Naboth's plot.
Scripture does not say which king of Israel is meant in the stories of 2 Kings 5–8.
Kings gives no age for him and no mother's name in his record; Jehu speaks of “thy mother Jezebel” (2 Kings 9:22).
Kings calls him both “Jehoram” and “Joram”; at the same time Jehoram (Joram) son of Jehoshaphat reigned in Judah. 2 Kings 1:17 2 Kings 8:16

From the text2 Kings 5–8 speaks only of “the king of Israel” (Naaman's letter, the Syrian raids, the siege of Samaria, the Shunammite's land). These chapters stand between Joram's accession (3:1) and his death (9:24); Scripture does not name the king in them.
